paper.title: Dogs (Canis familiaris) distinguish conspecific emotional chemosignals

summary.family_size_note: lower bound; unreported comparisons and the side-bias/period regressions have no reported p-value

claims.claim: Dogs distinguish conspecific odours collected under different emotion-eliciting conditions
claims.test_as_stated: Wilcoxon signed-rank, pooled (V=2704, p=0.008; V=2061.5, p<0.001)

findings.observed: the pooled test stacks 122 dog x pairing rows from 43 dogs
findings.fix: test one value per dog; it was done and the claim holds

claims.claim: Dogs did not distinguish stress from baseline odour

reanalysis.note: no interval or equivalence test reported or computable as an equivalence claim

findings.observed: the Discussion states dogs 'did not distinguish' and builds three explanatory paragraphs on a p = 0.818 non-rejection
findings.fix: report the estimate with its interval and state what effect sizes remain admissible

claims.claim: Stress odour increased proximity to the owner (secure-base claim)
claims.test_as_stated: Kruskal-Wallis H(2)=23.11, p<0.001 with Dunn post-hoc

findings.observed: the test ran on 12 dog-averaged time-bin means per condition; the 24 dogs appear only in the raw block and were never tested
findings.fix: test the 24 dogs; p moves from 9.6e-06 to 0.231

findings.observed: 12 consecutive 5-second bins of the same 6-9 dogs are treated as independent observations
findings.fix: treat the bins as repeated measures of a dog

findings.observed: Fig 6 reports 'means of the 12 sample points +/- S.E.M.'; over dogs the 95% interval for the blank condition is 2.9x wider
findings.fix: state the interval over the experimental unit

findings.observed: the supporting Dunn p-values are one-tailed; recomputed two-sided they are exactly double

claims.claim: Females responded more strongly to stress odour than males
claims.test_as_stated: Gaussian GLM, condition x sex (4 coefficients, p = 0.007 to <0.001)

findings.observed: fitted on 72 bin means (12 bins x 3 conditions x 2 sexes); the interaction rests on 4 female versus 5 male dogs in the stress condition
findings.fix: fit on dogs; all four interaction p-values move to 0.18-0.48

findings.observed: reported as a finding about sex differences in canine olfactory response rather than as a hypothesis
findings.fix: state it as not estimable at this n

findings_against_the_paper_as_a_whole.observed: 39 reported p-values with no correction named anywhere; Bonferroni removes 15 of 33, BH removes 2
findings_against_the_paper_as_a_whole.fix: declare the family and report corrected values

findings_against_the_paper_as_a_whole.observed: Shapiro-Wilk used as a switch between ANOVA and Kruskal-Wallis, applied to the 12 bin means
findings_against_the_paper_as_a_whole.fix: choose the test from the design; here the choice changes no conclusion

findings_against_the_paper_as_a_whole.observed: 'Any unreported comparisons showed no statistical significance (p>0.05)'; the posture analysis is described as prompted by an observation during coding and reported at the same alpha
findings_against_the_paper_as_a_whole.fix: state the total number of comparisons and label post-hoc analyses

findings_against_the_paper_as_a_whole.observed: the claim is about 'dogs'; the sample is 43 owner-recruited dogs at one laboratory and all odour stimuli came from a single female donor
findings_against_the_paper_as_a_whole.fix: state the population the evidence supports

findings_against_the_paper_as_a_whole.observed: an owner-distraction task was added partway through and the testing room changed; both dismissed as 'p>0.05' with no coefficient, interval or power statement on groups of 14/17/12
findings_against_the_paper_as_a_whole.fix: report the confounder estimate with its interval

findings_against_the_paper_as_a_whole.observed: the direction of V is unstated and flips within one paragraph (2704 + 4799 = 7503 = 122*123/2)

rules_passed.S4: every n in the paper reconciles exactly against the deposit
rules_passed.S9: the surviving Part 1 claims do not depend on signed-rank symmetry; sign test p = 0.0137 and 0.00027 agree with signed-rank despite skewness 1.15
rules_passed.S11: no reported p-value is below its resolution floor; smallest comparison has 17 non-zero pairs, floor 1.5e-05
rules_passed.S10: not applicable; no permutation or bootstrap used
rules_passed.S15: the abstract's Part 1 sentences match the tests supporting them

not_checked: behavioural coding (videos not deposited); inter-observer reliability not reported
per-condition entry counts for Part 2 before the 2 exclusions - not recoverable from the deposit
the size of the undeclared test family - side-bias and period regression p-values are not reported
chemical characterisation of the odour stimuli - none reported; a design question, noted not scored
